accounts.text: Pam and Clint are regular evening customers. Their custom helps keep my business going. I see Pam drink too much beer and remind myself not to judge my customers.
I was laid off from my job driving the bus. I would like to have that work back.
Gus gives me beer on my birthday, and I think well of him.
Penny is my only child. I want people to treat her kindly, hope she has a good life, and feel glad that she is clever and loves books.
I keep returning to the Saloon and look forward to a drink. I also think that ending up there so often is unhealthy, and wish I had another hobby; perhaps checkers on my own.
I used to drive a truck around the valley, meeting people and listening to the radio. I miss that work.
Pam used to drive the bus, which stopped working. She is out of work, and saving money from my tutoring has been difficult.
I worry that my mother does not look after herself. I want her to be happy, but that worry burdens me and I want a life outside this home.
My father left when I was a child. He said he felt trapped, and we have not seen him since. Autumn brings this memory back.
Reading helps me set aside the difficulties of my life for a while.
Pam often goes to the Saloon. I keep cleaning and doing the dishes alone; I connect her headaches and lack of help to those late nights.
I teach Vincent and Jas and try to give them opportunities to do well.
